shorts.title: What you will learn: Mini project: calculator
shorts.hook: Build a real calculator from small functions.
shorts.script: Build a real calculator from small functions. Today we build a mini project. You will join functions, input and switch into a working calculator. Good programs are made of small functions. Each function does one job. Main only joins them together. Our calculator has three jobs. First, read the numbers and the sign. Second, calculate. Third, print the answer. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: This function turns kilometres into miles.
shorts.script: This function turns kilometres into miles. This one turns Celsius into Fahrenheit. Ten kilometres is about six point two one miles. Thirty degrees Celsius is eighty-six degrees Fahrenheit. Each function has one small job, so they are easy to test. The program prints six point two one three seven one, and then eighty-six. Plan the functions before you write the code. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A function that forgets to return
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in a mini project, a calculator?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in a mini project, a calculator? Bug of the Day. The calc function handles only plus and minus. For any other sign, it reaches the end with no return. The compiler warns about control reaching the end of a non-void function. Add a final return for every other path. If op is neither plus nor minus, the function reaches the end without a return. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: A function that forgets to return.
